title: The Password Rules You Hate Came From One Guy's Guess
description:
Capital letter, number, symbol, change it every 90 days. That whole system traces back to one 2003 government document, and the man who wrote it later said he got it wrong.

#shorts #techfacts #cybersecurity

scenes.text: Almost every annoying password rule you've ever followed traces back to one document from 2003.
It was written by a manager at the US government's standards agency, based mostly on his own best guess.
The rules called for mixing capital letters, numbers, and symbols, and changing your password every few months.
In 2017, he publicly said he regretted it. Research since then shows those rules often push people toward weaker, more predictable passwords.
The updated official guidance now favors long passphrases over complex short ones, since length matters more than symbols.
So if your workplace still forces a new password every ninety days, that policy is running on outdated advice.
